sub_answers.text: Results of each of the 12 shows were determined by a 50/50 combination of votes from a jury panel and public televoting.[d40165141s3p0] The jury votes in all shows consisted of a combination of a Lithuanian jury panel and an international jury panel.[d40165141s3p0] From the second show to the semi-final the Lithuanian panel came to a consensus to assign one set of points which were added to the international panel results, while international panel members assigned points individually in descending order for their preferences.[d40165141s3p0] In the final the Lithuanian and international panels voted together with each member awarding one set of points based on ranking.[d40165141s3p0] The public vote ranking was converted to points from 1–8, 10 and 12 and assigned based on the number of competing artists in the respective show.[d40165141s3p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: What tie-breaking procedures and qualification criteria were specified for advancing between heats, semifinals, and the final?
sub_answers.text: Ties in the elimination shows and the semi-final were decided in favour of the entry that received the most votes from the public.[d40165141s3p0] In the final, a tie was decided in favour of the entry that was awarded the most points by the jury.[d40165141s3p0] The competition structure specified eliminations by show: the second and third shows featured ten artists each with five eliminated from each show,[d40165141s3p0] during each of the fourth to tenth shows one artist was eliminated and the remaining three artists advanced from those shows,[d40165141s3p0] and the eleventh show (semi-final) selected the single winning song from the remaining three songs while the twelfth show (final) selected the winning artist–song combination from the remaining three artists.[d40165141s3p0]

sub_answers.text: The results of each of the 12 shows were determined by a 50/50 combination of votes from a jury panel and public televoting [d40165141s3p0]. The jury votes in all shows consisted of a combination of a Lithuanian jury panel and an international jury panel, with the Lithuanian and international panels varying their voting method by round [d40165141s3p0]. From the second show to the semi-final the Lithuanian panel was required to come to a consensus to assign one set of points which were added to the international panel results, while the international panel members assigned points in descending order for their rankings [d40165141s3p0]. The Lithuanian panel assigned scores from 1 to 10 to each artist from the second to the fifth shows and assigned points based on ranking starting from the sixth show, and in the final the Lithuanian and international panels voted together with each member awarding one set of points based on ranking [d40165141s3p0]. Public voting (telephone and SMS) rankings were converted to points from 1-8, 10 and 12 and assigned based on the number of competing artists in the respective show [d40165141s3p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What procedures did the competition rules prescribe for resolving tied scores and for determining which acts advanced from heats to semifinals and from semifinals to the final (e.g., highest televote, jury preference, run-off), including any quotas or wildcard provisions?
sub_answers.text: The second and third shows each featured ten artists and five were eliminated from each of those shows [d40165141s3p0]. During each of the fourth to tenth shows one artist was eliminated and the remaining three artists advanced in the competition for those rounds [d40165141s3p0]. Starting from the fifth show the 16 potential Eurovision songs competed weekly and 13 songs were eliminated following the tenth show, leaving three songs for the semi-final [d40165141s3p0]. The eleventh show (semi-final) selected only the winning song from the remaining three songs, and the twelfth show (final) selected the winning artist–song combination from the remaining three artists [d40165141s3p0]. Ties in the elimination shows and the semi-final were decided in favour of the entry that received the most public votes, while ties in the final were decided in favour of the entry that was awarded the most points by the jury [d40165141s3p0].

sub_answers.text: The results in each of the 12 shows were determined by a 50/50 combination of votes from a jury panel and public televoting [d40165141s3p0]. The jury vote in all shows consisted of a combination of a Lithuanian jury panel and an international jury panel, with the international panel members assigning points in descending order for their favourites and the Lithuanian panel producing one set of points (by consensus from shows 2–semi) which was added to the international panel results [d40165141s3p0]. From shows 2–5 the Lithuanian panel assigned scores from 1 to 10 to each artist and from show 6 onward assigned points based on ranking; in the final the Lithuanian and international panels voted together, each member awarding one set of points based on ranking [d40165141s3p0]. The public could vote through telephone and SMS, and both jury and public rankings were converted to Eurovision-style points (1–8, 10 and 12) assigned based on the number of competing artists in the respective show [d40165141s3p0].
